The mechanism below is fixed. Add what holds it together, how
loads reach the world, and in what order it goes together.

Do not add or rename bodies, groups, joints, interfaces or configurations. If
something is missing, say so in unresolved.

1. WHAT HOLDS EACH BODY. For each body that must stay where it is put, state
   what stops it, as a constraint_relation below. ONE relation per (retained
   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline
   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION
   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. A relation that names no configuration
   therefore holds nowhere, so name them. A mechanism in which nothing is blocked
   is a pile of loose parts.
2. IRRELEVANCE. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the
   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a
   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need
   none.
3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,
   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the
   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a
   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from
   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and
   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.
   Never say how much load anything carries.
4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and
   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the
   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,
   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. NONE is the fourth value and it is not a strategy: it
   says nothing retains this body, which is the right answer for a part that is
   meant to come back out or that no constraint relation holds, and is not an
   answer for a body you have just declared a constraint_relation retains. Every
   body whose group appears as a `retained_group` above needs one of the three.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return one JSON object. Emit every key. Use exactly these key names.

  irrelevance[]         rigid_group, configuration, dof[], scenario
  physical_interactions[]
                        id "PHI-0001", groups[], effect, discharges_effect,
                        at_interface (optional), configurations[] (optional)
  constraint_relations[]
                        id "CRL-0001", retained_group, blocked_dofs[],
                        configurations[], driver, blocked_direction (optional),
                        provider_body (optional),
                        provider_reaction_site (optional),
                        provider_site (optional),
                        maintaining_interaction (optional),
                        defeat_specification (optional)
                        AT LEAST ONE of provider_body / provider_reaction_site
                        must identify what provides the constraint.
                        provider_site is where it acts and does not answer that.
  load_paths[]          id "LDP-0001", load_case, ordered_hops[],
                        terminates_at (optional)
                        The candidate is NOT yours to state: this pass is run
                        once per candidate and the one you are embodying is
                        named above, so the path is written against it.
  assembly_steps[]      id "ASY-0001", order_index, body, access_side,
                        activates[], termination_strategy, path_kind, depends_on[]
  unresolved[]          id "S3U-1001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                        alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

  blocked_direction     +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE
  provider_body         a body id, not a description
  configurations        configuration ids where the relation holds
  blocked_dofs          which of TX TY TZ RX RY RZ the relation removes
  driver                LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO
  defeat_specification  how a test would defeat this constraint
  termination_strategy  LATER_BODY_COVER | ROTATION | ELASTICITY | NONE
  path_kind             RIGID | DEFORMATION_RESOLVED
  alternatives_kind     ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT

PHYSICAL REALIZATION
This candidate must physically do what the input's PHYSICAL EFFECT OBLIGATIONS
require. Those obligations are candidate-independent: they say WHAT effect must
occur, between which roles. You say HOW THIS CANDIDATE does it.

  For every effect obligation this candidate realizes, emit a
  physical_interaction naming the rigid groups between which the effect passes,
  the effect (TRANSMIT_FORCE | TRANSMIT_MOTION | CONVERT_MOTION | PERMIT_MOTION | PREVENT_MOTION | LOCATE | CONTAIN | METER), and the obligation id it discharges. An interaction
  TRANSMITS; a joint CONSTRAINS. They are not the same fact and a joint is not a
  substitute for one.

  For every constraint this candidate relies on, emit a constraint_relation: the
  retained group, which DOFs it removes, in which configurations, and what
  DRIVES it (LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO). Name what PROVIDES it - a body of this mechanism in
  provider_body, or, where the reaction is taken outside the product, the
  declared reaction site in provider_reaction_site. Those are the two kinds of
  provider there are; the world is not a body. provider_site is a different
  fact: the interface of this mechanism at which the constraint acts. Do not
  leave a constraint standing on nothing, and do not report one you have not
  decided.

  For every load case, emit a load_path: the ordered interfaces the load passes
  through, and where it terminates. If the load reaches a declared EXTERNAL
  reaction site, name it in terminates_at. If it does not, leave terminates_at
  out - an open path is a real answer and saying so is better than closing it
  with something you did not establish.

REFERENCES BETWEEN ITEMS

  physical_interactions[].at_interface

rendered prompt (50933 chars)

The mechanism below is fixed. Add what holds it together, how
loads reach the world, and in what order it goes together.

Do not add or rename bodies, groups, joints, interfaces or configurations. If
something is missing, say so in unresolved.

1. WHAT HOLDS EACH BODY. For each body that must stay where it is put, state
   what stops it, as a constraint_relation below. ONE relation per (retained
   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline
   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION
   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. A relation that names no configuration
   therefore holds nowhere, so name them. A mechanism in which nothing is blocked
   is a pile of loose parts.
2. IRRELEVANCE. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the
   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a
   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need
   none.
3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,
   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the
   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a
   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from
   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and
   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.
   Never say how much load anything carries.
4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and
   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the
   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,
   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. NONE is the fourth value and it is not a strategy: it
   says nothing retains this body, which is the right answer for a part that is
   meant to come back out or that no constraint relation holds, and is not an
   answer for a body you have just declared a constraint_relation retains. Every
   body whose group appears as a `retained_group` above needs one of the three.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return one JSON object. Emit every key. Use exactly these key names.

  irrelevance[]         rigid_group, configuration, dof[], scenario
  physical_interactions[]
                        id "PHI-0001", groups[], effect, discharges_effect,
                        at_interface (optional), configurations[] (optional)
  constraint_relations[]
                        id "CRL-0001", retained_group, blocked_dofs[],
                        configurations[], driver, blocked_direction (optional),
                        provider_body (optional),
                        provider_reaction_site (optional),
                        provider_site (optional),
                        maintaining_interaction (optional),
                        defeat_specification (optional)
                        AT LEAST ONE of provider_body / provider_reaction_site
                        must identify what provides the constraint.
                        provider_site is where it acts and does not answer that.
  load_paths[]          id "LDP-0001", load_case, ordered_hops[],
                        terminates_at (optional)
                        The candidate is NOT yours to state: this pass is run
                        once per candidate and the one you are embodying is
                        named above, so the path is written against it.
  assembly_steps[]      id "ASY-0001", order_index, body, access_side,
                        activates[], termination_strategy, path_kind, depends_on[]
  unresolved[]          id "S3U-1001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                        alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

  blocked_direction     +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE
  provider_body         a body id, not a description
  configurations        configuration ids where the relation holds
  blocked_dofs          which of TX TY TZ RX RY RZ the relation removes
  driver                LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO
  defeat_specification  how a test would defeat this constraint
  termination_strategy  LATER_BODY_COVER | ROTATION | ELASTICITY | NONE
  path_kind             RIGID | DEFORMATION_RESOLVED
  alternatives_kind     ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT

PHYSICAL REALIZATION
This candidate must physically do what the input's PHYSICAL EFFECT OBLIGATIONS
require. Those obligations are candidate-independent: they say WHAT effect must
occur, between which roles. You say HOW THIS CANDIDATE does it.

  For every effect obligation this candidate realizes, emit a
  physical_interaction naming the rigid groups between which the effect passes,
  the effect (TRANSMIT_FORCE | TRANSMIT_MOTION | CONVERT_MOTION | PERMIT_MOTION | PREVENT_MOTION | LOCATE | CONTAIN | METER), and the obligation id it discharges. An interaction
  TRANSMITS; a joint CONSTRAINS. They are not the same fact and a joint is not a
  substitute for one.

  For every constraint this candidate relies on, emit a constraint_relation: the
  retained group, which DOFs it removes, in which configurations, and what
  DRIVES it (LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO). Name what PROVIDES it - a body of this mechanism in
  provider_body, or, where the reaction is taken outside the product, the
  declared reaction site in provider_reaction_site. Those are the two kinds of
  provider there are; the world is not a body. provider_site is a different
  fact: the interface of this mechanism at which the constraint acts. Do not
  leave a constraint standing on nothing, and do not report one you have not
  decided.

  For every load case, emit a load_path: the ordered interfaces the load passes
  through, and where it terminates. If the load reaches a declared EXTERNAL
  reaction site, name it in terminates_at. If it does not, leave terminates_at
  out - an open path is a real answer and saying so is better than closing it
  with something you did not establish.

REFERENCES BETWEEN ITEMS
Every field below holds ENTITY IDS and nothing else. A description is
not an id: prose in one of these fields names no entity and is refused.
An id is either one from the TYPED INPUT below or one you create in this
same response, and it must be of the family named here - a body id where
a step is required denotes the wrong thing, however sensible it reads.

  assembly_steps[].activates
      Interface ids; [] when there are none
  assembly_steps[].body
      Body id
  assembly_steps[].depends_on
      AssemblyStep ids; [] when there are none
  constraint_relations[].configurations
      Configuration ids; [] when there are none
  constraint_relations[].maintaining_interaction
      PhysicalInteraction id
  constraint_relations[].provider_body
      Body id
  constraint_relations[].provider_reaction_site
      ReactionSiteRequirement id
  constraint_relations[].provider_site
      Interface id
  constraint_relations[].retained_group
      RigidGroup id
  load_paths[].load_case
      LoadCase id
  load_paths[].ordered_hops
      Interface ids; [] when there are none
  load_paths[].terminates_at
      ReactionSiteRequirement id
  physical_interactions[].at_interface
      Interface id
  physical_interactions[].configurations
      Configuration ids; [] when there are none
  physical_interactions[].discharges_effect
      PhysicalEffectObligation id
  physical_interactions[].groups
      RigidGroup ids; [] when there are none
  unresolved[].alternatives

rendered prompt (50486 chars)

The mechanism below is fixed. Add what holds it together, how
loads reach the world, and in what order it goes together.

Do not add or rename bodies, groups, joints, interfaces or configurations. If
something is missing, say so in unresolved.

1. WHAT HOLDS EACH BODY. For each body that must stay where it is put, state
   what stops it, as a constraint_relation below. ONE relation per (retained
   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline
   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION
   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. A relation that names no configuration
   therefore holds nowhere, so name them. A mechanism in which nothing is blocked
   is a pile of loose parts.
2. IRRELEVANCE. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the
   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a
   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need
   none.
3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,
   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the
   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a
   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from
   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and
   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.
   Never say how much load anything carries.
4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and
   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the
   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,
   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. NONE is the fourth value and it is not a strategy: it
   says nothing retains this body, which is the right answer for a part that is
   meant to come back out or that no constraint relation holds, and is not an
   answer for a body you have just declared a constraint_relation retains. Every
   body whose group appears as a `retained_group` above needs one of the three.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return one JSON object. Emit every key. Use exactly these key names.

  irrelevance[]         rigid_group, configuration, dof[], scenario
  physical_interactions[]
                        id "PHI-0001", groups[], effect, discharges_effect,
                        at_interface (optional), configurations[] (optional)
  constraint_relations[]
                        id "CRL-0001", retained_group, blocked_dofs[],
                        configurations[], driver, blocked_direction (optional),
                        provider_body (optional),
                        provider_reaction_site (optional),
                        provider_site (optional),
                        maintaining_interaction (optional),
                        defeat_specification (optional)
                        AT LEAST ONE of provider_body / provider_reaction_site
                        must identify what provides the constraint.
                        provider_site is where it acts and does not answer that.
  load_paths[]          id "LDP-0001", load_case, ordered_hops[],
                        terminates_at (optional)
                        The candidate is NOT yours to state: this pass is run
                        once per candidate and the one you are embodying is
                        named above, so the path is written against it.
  assembly_steps[]      id "ASY-0001", order_index, body, access_side,
                        activates[], termination_strategy, path_kind, depends_on[]
  unresolved[]          id "S3U-1001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                        alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

  blocked_direction     +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE
  provider_body         a body id, not a description
  configurations        configuration ids where the relation holds
  blocked_dofs          which of TX TY TZ RX RY RZ the relation removes
  driver                LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO
  defeat_specification  how a test would defeat this constraint
  termination_strategy  LATER_BODY_COVER | ROTATION | ELASTICITY | NONE
  path_kind             RIGID | DEFORMATION_RESOLVED
  alternatives_kind     ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT

PHYSICAL REALIZATION
This candidate must physically do what the input's PHYSICAL EFFECT OBLIGATIONS
require. Those obligations are candidate-independent: they say WHAT effect must
occur, between which roles. You say HOW THIS CANDIDATE does it.

  For every effect obligation this candidate realizes, emit a
  physical_interaction naming the rigid groups between which the effect passes,
  the effect (TRANSMIT_FORCE | TRANSMIT_MOTION | CONVERT_MOTION | PERMIT_MOTION | PREVENT_MOTION | LOCATE | CONTAIN | METER), and the obligation id it discharges. An interaction
  TRANSMITS; a joint CONSTRAINS. They are not the same fact and a joint is not a
  substitute for one.

  For every constraint this candidate relies on, emit a constraint_relation: the
  retained group, which DOFs it removes, in which configurations, and what
  DRIVES it (LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO). Name what PROVIDES it - a body of this mechanism in
  provider_body, or, where the reaction is taken outside the product, the
  declared reaction site in provider_reaction_site. Those are the two kinds of
  provider there are; the world is not a body. provider_site is a different
  fact: the interface of this mechanism at which the constraint acts. Do not
  leave a constraint standing on nothing, and do not report one you have not
  decided.

  For every load case, emit a load_path: the ordered interfaces the load passes
  through, and where it terminates. If the load reaches a declared EXTERNAL
  reaction site, name it in terminates_at. If it does not, leave terminates_at
  out - an open path is a real answer and saying so is better than closing it
  with something you did not establish.

ONE relation per (retained\n   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline\n   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION\n   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the\n   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a\n   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need\n   none.\n3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,\n   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the\n   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a\n   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from\n   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and\n   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.\n   Never say how much load anything carries.\n4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and\n   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the\n   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,\n   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. rendered prompt (46470 chars)

The mechanism below is fixed. Add what holds it together, how
loads reach the world, and in what order it goes together.

Do not add or rename bodies, groups, joints, interfaces or configurations. If
something is missing, say so in unresolved.

1. WHAT HOLDS EACH BODY. For each body that must stay where it is put, state
   what stops it, as a constraint_relation below. ONE relation per (retained
   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline
   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION
   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. A relation that names no configuration
   therefore holds nowhere, so name them. A mechanism in which nothing is blocked
   is a pile of loose parts.
2. IRRELEVANCE. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the
   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a
   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need
   none.
3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,
   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the
   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a
   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from
   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and
   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.
   Never say how much load anything carries.
4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and
   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the
   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,
   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. NONE is the fourth value and it is not a strategy: it
   says nothing retains this body, which is the right answer for a part that is
   meant to come back out or that no constraint relation holds, and is not an
   answer for a body you have just declared a constraint_relation retains. Every
   body whose group appears as a `retained_group` above needs one of the three.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return one JSON object. Emit every key. Use exactly these key names.

  irrelevance[]         rigid_group, configuration, dof[], scenario
  physical_interactions[]
                        id "PHI-0001", groups[], effect, discharges_effect,
                        at_interface (optional), configurations[] (optional)
  constraint_relations[]
                        id "CRL-0001", retained_group, blocked_dofs[],
                        configurations[], driver, blocked_direction (optional),
                        provider_body (optional),
                        provider_reaction_site (optional),
                        provider_site (optional),
                        maintaining_interaction (optional),
                        defeat_specification (optional)
                        AT LEAST ONE of provider_body / provider_reaction_site
                        must identify what provides the constraint.
                        provider_site is where it acts and does not answer that.
  load_paths[]          id "LDP-0001", load_case, ordered_hops[],
                        terminates_at (optional)
                        The candidate is NOT yours to state: this pass is run
                        once per candidate and the one you are embodying is
                        named above, so the path is written against it.
  assembly_steps[]      id "ASY-0001", order_index, body, access_side,
                        activates[], termination_strategy, path_kind, depends_on[]
  unresolved[]          id "S3U-1001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                        alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

  blocked_direction     +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE
  provider_body         a body id, not a description
  configurations        configuration ids where the relation holds
  blocked_dofs          which of TX TY TZ RX RY RZ the relation removes
  driver                LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO
  defeat_specification  how a test would defeat this constraint
  termination_strategy  LATER_BODY_COVER | ROTATION | ELASTICITY | NONE
  path_kind             RIGID | DEFORMATION_RESOLVED
  alternatives_kind     ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT

PHYSICAL REALIZATION
This candidate must physically do what the input's PHYSICAL EFFECT OBLIGATIONS
require. Those obligations are candidate-independent: they say WHAT effect must
occur, between which roles. You say HOW THIS CANDIDATE does it.

  For every effect obligation this candidate realizes, emit a
  physical_interaction naming the rigid groups between which the effect passes,
  the effect (TRANSMIT_FORCE | TRANSMIT_MOTION | CONVERT_MOTION | PERMIT_MOTION | PREVENT_MOTION | LOCATE | CONTAIN | METER), and the obligation id it discharges. An interaction
  TRANSMITS; a joint CONSTRAINS. They are not the same fact and a joint is not a
  substitute for one.

  For every constraint this candidate relies on, emit a constraint_relation: the
  retained group, which DOFs it removes, in which configurations, and what
  DRIVES it (LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO). Name what PROVIDES it - a body of this mechanism in
  provider_body, or, where the reaction is taken outside the product, the
  declared reaction site in provider_reaction_site. Those are the two kinds of
  provider there are; the world is not a body. provider_site is a different
  fact: the interface of this mechanism at which the constraint acts. Do not
  leave a constraint standing on nothing, and do not report one you have not
  decided.

  For every load case, emit a load_path: the ordered interfaces the load passes
  through, and where it terminates. If the load reaches a declared EXTERNAL
  reaction site, name it in terminates_at. If it does not, leave terminates_at
  out - an open path is a real answer and saying so is better than closing it
  with something you did not establish.

REFERENCES BETWEEN ITEMS

not an id: prose in one of these fields names no entity and is refused.

  unresolved[].alternatives

Add what holds it together, how\nloads reach the world, and in what order it goes together.\n\nDo not add or rename bodies, groups, joints, interfaces or configurations. ONE relation per (retained\n   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline\n   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION\n   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. A relation that names no configuration\n   therefore holds nowhere, so name them. A mechanism in which nothing is blocked\n   is a pile of loose parts.\n2. IRRELEVANCE. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the\n   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a\n   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need\n   none.\n3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,\n   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the\n   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a\n   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from\n   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and\n   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.\n   Never say how much load anything carries.\n4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and\n   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the\n   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,\n   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. rendered prompt (49057 chars)

The mechanism below is fixed. Add what holds it together, how
loads reach the world, and in what order it goes together.

Do not add or rename bodies, groups, joints, interfaces or configurations. If
something is missing, say so in unresolved.

1. WHAT HOLDS EACH BODY. For each body that must stay where it is put, state
   what stops it, as a constraint_relation below. ONE relation per (retained
   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline
   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION
   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. A relation that names no configuration
   therefore holds nowhere, so name them. A mechanism in which nothing is blocked
   is a pile of loose parts.
2. IRRELEVANCE. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the
   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a
   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need
   none.
3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,
   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the
   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a
   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from
   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and
   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.
   Never say how much load anything carries.
4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and
   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the
   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,
   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. NONE is the fourth value and it is not a strategy: it
   says nothing retains this body, which is the right answer for a part that is
   meant to come back out or that no constraint relation holds, and is not an
   answer for a body you have just declared a constraint_relation retains. Every
   body whose group appears as a `retained_group` above needs one of the three.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return one JSON object. Emit every key. Use exactly these key names.

  irrelevance[]         rigid_group, configuration, dof[], scenario
  physical_interactions[]
                        id "PHI-0001", groups[], effect, discharges_effect,
                        at_interface (optional), configurations[] (optional)
  constraint_relations[]
                        id "CRL-0001", retained_group, blocked_dofs[],
                        configurations[], driver, blocked_direction (optional),
                        provider_body (optional),
                        provider_reaction_site (optional),
                        provider_site (optional),
                        maintaining_interaction (optional),
                        defeat_specification (optional)
                        AT LEAST ONE of provider_body / provider_reaction_site
                        must identify what provides the constraint.
                        provider_site is where it acts and does not answer that.
  load_paths[]          id "LDP-0001", load_case, ordered_hops[],
                        terminates_at (optional)
                        The candidate is NOT yours to state: this pass is run
                        once per candidate and the one you are embodying is
                        named above, so the path is written against it.
  assembly_steps[]      id "ASY-0001", order_index, body, access_side,
                        activates[], termination_strategy, path_kind, depends_on[]
  unresolved[]          id "S3U-1001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                        alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

  blocked_direction     +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE
  provider_body         a body id, not a description
  configurations        configuration ids where the relation holds
  blocked_dofs          which of TX TY TZ RX RY RZ the relation removes
  driver                LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO
  defeat_specification  how a test would defeat this constraint
  termination_strategy  LATER_BODY_COVER | ROTATION | ELASTICITY | NONE
  path_kind             RIGID | DEFORMATION_RESOLVED
  alternatives_kind     ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT

PHYSICAL REALIZATION
This candidate must physically do what the input's PHYSICAL EFFECT OBLIGATIONS
require. Those obligations are candidate-independent: they say WHAT effect must
occur, between which roles. You say HOW THIS CANDIDATE does it.

  For every effect obligation this candidate realizes, emit a
  physical_interaction naming the rigid groups between which the effect passes,
  the effect (TRANSMIT_FORCE | TRANSMIT_MOTION | CONVERT_MOTION | PERMIT_MOTION | PREVENT_MOTION | LOCATE | CONTAIN | METER), and the obligation id it discharges. An interaction
  TRANSMITS; a joint CONSTRAINS. They are not the same fact and a joint is not a
  substitute for one.

  For every constraint this candidate relies on, emit a constraint_relation: the
  retained group, which DOFs it removes, in which configurations, and what
  DRIVES it (LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO). Name what PROVIDES it - a body of this mechanism in
  provider_body, or, where the reaction is taken outside the product, the
  declared reaction site in provider_reaction_site. Those are the two kinds of
  provider there are; the world is not a body. provider_site is a different
  fact: the interface of this mechanism at which the constraint acts. Do not
  leave a constraint standing on nothing, and do not report one you have not
  decided.

  For every load case, emit a load_path: the ordered interfaces the load passes
  through, and where it terminates. If the load reaches a declared EXTERNAL
  reaction site, name it in terminates_at. If it does not, leave terminates_at
  out - an open path is a real answer and saying so is better than closing it
  with something you did not establish.

REFERENCES BETWEEN ITEMS
Every field below holds ENTITY IDS and nothing else. A description is
not an id: prose in one of these fields names no entity and is refused.
An id is either one from the TYPED INPUT below or one you create in this
same response, and it must be of the family named here - a body id where
a step is required denotes the wrong thing, however sensible it reads.

  assembly_steps[].activates

  assembly_steps[].body
      Body id
  assembly_steps[].depends_on
      AssemblyStep ids; [] when there are none
  constraint_relations[].configurations
      Configuration ids; [] when there are none

      PhysicalInteraction id
  constraint_relations[].provider_body
      Body id
  constraint_relations[].provider_reaction_site
      ReactionSiteRequirement id
  constraint_relations[].provider_site
      Interface id
  constraint_relations[].retained_group
      RigidGroup id
  load_paths[].load_case
      LoadCase id
  load_paths[].ordered_hops
      Interface ids; [] when there are none
  load_paths[].terminates_at
      ReactionSiteRequirement id
  physical_interactions[].at_interface
      Interface id
  physical_interactions[].configurations
      Configuration ids; [] when there are none
  physical_interactions[].discharges_effect
      PhysicalEffectObligation id
  physical_interactions[].groups
      RigidGroup ids; [] when there are none
  unresolved[].alternatives
      ONLY when alternatives_kind is ENTITY_REFS: any entity id this design has
      - the field is deliberately not restricted to one family, and prose is
      still refused. Otherwise this field holds no ids at all and nothing here
      applies to it
  unresolved[].blocks
      any entity id this design has - the field is deliberately not restricted
      to one family, and prose is still refused
  unresolved[].kept_open_by
      Ambiguity or Freedom ids - either family, and nothing else; [] when there
      are none

    "prompt_text": "The mechanism below is fixed. Add what holds it together, how\nloads reach the world, and in what order it goes together.\n\nDo not add or rename bodies, groups, joints, interfaces or configurations. If\nsomething is missing, say so in unresolved.\n\n1. WHAT HOLDS EACH BODY. For each body that must stay where it is put, state\n   what stops it, as a constraint_relation below. ONE relation per (retained\n   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline\n   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION\n   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. A relation that names no configuration\n   therefore holds nowhere, so name them. A mechanism in which nothing is blocked\n   is a pile of loose parts.\n2. IRRELEVANCE. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the\n   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a\n   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need\n   none.\n3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,\n   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the\n   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a\n   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from\n   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and\n   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.\n   Never say how much load anything carries.\n4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and\n   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the\n   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,\n   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. NONE is the fourth value and it is not a strategy: it\n   says nothing retains this body, which is the right answer for a part that is\n   meant to come back out or that no constraint relation holds, and is not an\n   answer for a body you have just declared a constraint_relation retains. Every\n   body whose group appears as a `retained_group` above needs one of the three.\n\nRESPONSE SCHEMA\nReturn one JSON object. Emit every key. Use exactly these key names.\n\n  irrelevance[]         rigid_group, configuration, dof[], scenario\n  physical_interactions[]\n                        id \"PHI-0001\", groups[], effect, discharges_effect,\n                        at_interface (optional), configurations[] (optional)\n  constraint_relations[]\n                        id \"CRL-0001\", retained_group, blocked_dofs[],\n                        configurations[], driver, blocked_direction (optional),\n                        provider_body (optional),\n                        provider_reaction_site (optional),\n                        provider_site (optional),\n                        maintaining_interaction (optional),\n                        defeat_specification (optional)\n                        AT LEAST ONE of provider_body / provider_reaction_site\n                        must identify what provides the constraint.\n                        provider_site is where it acts and does not answer that.\n  load_paths[]          id \"LDP-0001\", load_case, ordered_hops[],\n                        terminates_at (optional)\n                        The candidate is NOT yours to state: this pass is run\n                        once per candidate and the one you are embodying is\n                        named above, so the path is written against it.\n  assembly_steps[]      id \"ASY-0001\", order_index, body, access_side,\n                        activates[], termination_strategy, path_kind, depends_on[]\n  unresolved[]          id \"S3U-1001\", decision, why_open, alternatives[],\n                        alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]\n\n  blocked_direction     +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE\n  provider_body         a body id, not a description\n  configurations rendered prompt (52080 chars)

The mechanism below is fixed. Add what holds it together, how
loads reach the world, and in what order it goes together.

Do not add or rename bodies, groups, joints, interfaces or configurations. If
something is missing, say so in unresolved.

1. WHAT HOLDS EACH BODY. For each body that must stay where it is put, state
   what stops it, as a constraint_relation below. ONE relation per (retained
   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline
   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION
   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. A relation that names no configuration
   therefore holds nowhere, so name them. A mechanism in which nothing is blocked
   is a pile of loose parts.
2. IRRELEVANCE. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the
   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a
   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need
   none.
3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,
   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the
   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a
   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from
   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and
   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.
   Never say how much load anything carries.
4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and
   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the
   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,
   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. NONE is the fourth value and it is not a strategy: it
   says nothing retains this body, which is the right answer for a part that is
   meant to come back out or that no constraint relation holds, and is not an
   answer for a body you have just declared a constraint_relation retains. Every
   body whose group appears as a `retained_group` above needs one of the three.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return one JSON object. Emit every key. Use exactly these key names.

  irrelevance[]         rigid_group, configuration, dof[], scenario
  physical_interactions[]
                        id "PHI-0001", groups[], effect, discharges_effect,
                        at_interface (optional), configurations[] (optional)
  constraint_relations[]
                        id "CRL-0001", retained_group, blocked_dofs[],
                        configurations[], driver, blocked_direction (optional),
                        provider_body (optional),
                        provider_reaction_site (optional),
                        provider_site (optional),
                        maintaining_interaction (optional),
                        defeat_specification (optional)
                        AT LEAST ONE of provider_body / provider_reaction_site
                        must identify what provides the constraint.
                        provider_site is where it acts and does not answer that.
  load_paths[]          id "LDP-0001", load_case, ordered_hops[],
                        terminates_at (optional)
                        The candidate is NOT yours to state: this pass is run
                        once per candidate and the one you are embodying is
                        named above, so the path is written against it.
  assembly_steps[]      id "ASY-0001", order_index, body, access_side,
                        activates[], termination_strategy, path_kind, depends_on[]
  unresolved[]          id "S3U-1001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                        alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

  blocked_direction     +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE
  provider_body         a body id, not a description
  configurations        configuration ids where the relation holds
  blocked_dofs          which of TX TY TZ RX RY RZ the relation removes
  driver                LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO
  defeat_specification  how a test would defeat this constraint
  termination_strategy  LATER_BODY_COVER | ROTATION | ELASTICITY | NONE
  path_kind             RIGID | DEFORMATION_RESOLVED
  alternatives_kind     ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT

PHYSICAL REALIZATION
This candidate must physically do what the input's PHYSICAL EFFECT OBLIGATIONS
require. Those obligations are candidate-independent: they say WHAT effect must
occur, between which roles. You say HOW THIS CANDIDATE does it.

  For every effect obligation this candidate realizes, emit a
  physical_interaction naming the rigid groups between which the effect passes,
  the effect (TRANSMIT_FORCE | TRANSMIT_MOTION | CONVERT_MOTION | PERMIT_MOTION | PREVENT_MOTION | LOCATE | CONTAIN | METER), and the obligation id it discharges. An interaction
  TRANSMITS; a joint CONSTRAINS. They are not the same fact and a joint is not a
  substitute for one.

  For every constraint this candidate relies on, emit a constraint_relation: the
  retained group, which DOFs it removes, in which configurations, and what
  DRIVES it (LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO). Name what PROVIDES it - a body of this mechanism in
  provider_body, or, where the reaction is taken outside the product, the
  declared reaction site in provider_reaction_site. Those are the two kinds of
  provider there are; the world is not a body. provider_site is a different
  fact: the interface of this mechanism at which the constraint acts. Do not
  leave a constraint standing on nothing, and do not report one you have not
  decided.

  For every load case, emit a load_path: the ordered interfaces the load passes
  through, and where it terminates. If the load reaches a declared EXTERNAL
  reaction site, name it in terminates_at. If it does not, leave terminates_at
  out - an open path is a real answer and saying so is better than closing it
  with something you did not establish.

REFERENCES BETWEEN ITEMS
Every field below holds ENTITY IDS and nothing else. A description is
not an id: prose in one of these fields names no entity and is refused.
An id is either one from the TYPED INPUT below or one you create in this
same response, and it must be of the family named here - a body id where
a step is required denotes the wrong thing, however sensible it reads.

  assembly_steps[].activates
      Interface ids; [] when there are none
  assembly_steps[].body
      Body id
  assembly_steps[].depends_on
      AssemblyStep ids; [] when there are none
  constraint_relations[].configurations
      Configuration ids; [] when there are none
  constraint_relations[].maintaining_interaction
      PhysicalInteraction id
  constraint_relations[].provider_body
      Body id
  constraint_relations[].provider_reaction_site
      ReactionSiteRequirement id
  constraint_relations[].provider_site
      Interface id
  constraint_relations[].retained_group
      RigidGroup id
  load_paths[].load_case
      LoadCase id
  load_paths[].ordered_hops
      Interface ids; [] when there are none
  load_paths[].terminates_at
      ReactionSiteRequirement id
  physical_interactions[].at_interface
      Interface id
  physical_interactions[].configurations
      Configuration ids; [] when there are none
  physical_interactions[].discharges_effect
      PhysicalEffectObligation id
  physical_interactions[].groups
      RigidGroup ids; [] when there are none
  unresolved[].alternatives
      ONLY when alternatives_kind is ENTITY_REFS: any entity id this design has
      - the field is deliberately not restricted to one family, and prose is
      still refused. Otherwise this field holds no ids at all and nothing here
      applies to it
  unresolved[].blocks
      any entity id this design has - the field is deliberately not restricted
      to one family, and prose is still refused
  unresolved[].kept_open_by
      Ambiguity or Freedom ids - either family, and nothing else; [] when there
      are none
